seoTitle: How to Increase Your Selling Limit on eBay
metaDescription: Learn how to check your eBay selling limit, request an increase, and build the seller history that helps eBay approve higher limits automatically.
intro: Every new or lower-volume eBay account is capped at a set number of items and total dollar value per month — it's how eBay manages risk while you build a track record. The limit isn't fixed forever, though, and there's a real request button sitting right where you'd check your current numbers. This guide follows that actual flow: finding your limit, requesting an increase, and understanding why eBay might turn the request down.

steps.heading: Open My eBay and find the Selling section
steps.body: From the My eBay dropdown, scroll past the buying-side items — Recently Viewed, Bids & Offers, Watchlist, Purchases — down to the Selling section, which expands to show Overview, Sell an Item, Drafts, Scheduled, Active, and Sold. Your selling limit isn't a separate hidden setting; it's tied directly to this same seller dashboard.

image.caption: The My eBay sidebar with Selling expanded, showing Overview, Sell an Item, Drafts, Scheduled, Active, and Sold.

steps.heading: Check your current monthly limit
steps.body: Your selling limits page states your usage plainly — for example, "Currently, you've listed or sold 0 items of your 10 monthly limit. You can list or sell up to $200.00 more to reach your $200.00 monthly limit." eBay explains this cap exists to help you grow your business in a manageable way and make sure you can meet buyer demand, with the promise that the limit increases as you demonstrate you can handle more volume reliably.

image.caption: The selling limits summary, showing items listed against the monthly cap with a "Request a limit increase" button directly below it.

steps.heading: Submit a request for a higher limit
steps.body: Click "Request a limit increase" directly on that same page — it's a single button, not a support ticket you have to open separately. eBay evaluates the request against your account automatically rather than routing every case to a human reviewer first, which is why the outcome often appears immediately rather than after a waiting period.

steps.heading: Understand why a request might get declined
steps.body: If your account doesn't yet qualify, you'll land on a page that says plainly: "Unfortunately, you're not currently eligible for a selling limit increase," with guidance to build up your selling history or wait until your current monthly limit resets before trying again. This isn't a permanent block — it's eBay's algorithm saying your account hasn't yet shown the volume or consistency it wants to see before raising the cap.

image.caption: The result screen for an ineligible request, explaining that building more selling history or waiting for the monthly reset are the next steps.

steps.heading: Build the account signals that support approval
steps.body: Between requests, focus on the things eBay explicitly weighs: completing sales without disputes, keeping your feedback score healthy, and letting your account age with consistent activity rather than long gaps. A verified PayPal account linked to your profile also supports your case, since it's one more signal that transactions on your account are legitimate and traceable.

steps.heading: Let automatic increases kick in over time
steps.body: You don't need to manually request every increase — eBay's system reviews seller accounts on an ongoing basis and can raise your limit automatically once your performance and feedback history clear its internal thresholds. Manually requesting is useful when you have a specific reason to need more room now, like a bulk purchase to resell, but steady, dispute-free selling is what moves the needle for the automatic increases over the following months.

faq.question: Where do I check my eBay selling limit?
faq.answer: Your current limit is shown on the selling limits page, reachable through My eBay's Selling section, along with a direct button to request an increase.

faq.question: How do I request a selling limit increase?
faq.answer: Click the "Request a limit increase" button shown right on your selling limits summary page — eBay evaluates it automatically against your account.

faq.question: What happens if my request is declined?
faq.answer: You'll see a message explaining you're not currently eligible, with guidance to build more selling history or wait for your monthly limit to reset before trying again.

faq.question: What factors influence limit approval?
faq.answer: Your performance history, feedback score, account age, and dispute-free sales are the key factors eBay considers, along with whether you have a verified PayPal account linked.

faq.question: Can my limit increase automatically over time?
faq.answer: Yes — eBay's system can grant automatic increases as your account builds a track record of consistent, dispute-free selling, without you needing to submit a manual request.
